value.answer: For most adults, short-term use looks safe. The NIH says that, though its page is from 2022, and UC Davis (Feb 2025) says it's typically safe and well tolerated at low doses when taken for the shortest time. Long term is the open question. A new American Heart Association abstract from November 2025 linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to more heart failure: 4.6% of long-term users vs 2.7% of non-users over five years, across 130,828 adults. It's preliminary and not peer-reviewed, and it can't prove cause, since poor sleep itself may be the driver. Sources also disagree on dose, so check with a doctor or pharmacist on how much and how long, especially if you take other meds.
